name: The Rust Prophets
description:
The Rust Prophets are what happens when augmentation addiction meets religious fervor. They're a crew of about thirty-five heavily modified individuals operating out of a condemned auto plant in Detroit's Delray district, and they believe — with the unshakeable certainty of the truly addicted — that the path to transcendence is through metal. More augments. More chrome. More replacement of weak flesh with strong steel. The fact that their bodies are rejecting the modifications, that half of them are running black-market immunosuppressants to keep their implants from killing them, that several members have augmented themselves past the point of being recognizably human — none of this registers as a problem. It registers as progress.

The Prophets fund their habit through a combination of augment theft, chop-shop surgery, and occasional mercenary work. They're not subtle operators. They hit augment clinics, rob couriers carrying implant shipments, and ambush lone travelers to strip them of whatever chrome they're carrying. The stolen augments either go into a Prophet or get sold to fund the next round of modifications. Their chop shop — a filthy operating theater in the back of the auto plant — installs augments at a fraction of legitimate cost, which attracts desperate clients willing to risk infection and rejection for affordable chrome.

What makes them dangerous isn't their numbers or their tactics. It's that they're unpredictable. Augmentation addiction degrades judgment, impulse control, and pain response. A Prophet in the grip of chrome hunger will do things that a rational operator wouldn't consider. They don't retreat when they should. They don't negotiate when they could. They escalate because their modified nervous systems are screaming for more input, more sensation, more metal.
ideology: Flesh is failure. The Rust Prophets believe that human evolution stalled and that augmentation is the next step — not the careful, measured augmentation of legitimate clinics, but the radical, total replacement of biology with machinery. Their leader, a figure known only as the Architect, preaches that consciousness will survive the complete replacement of the body. No one has tested this theory. Several Prophets are getting close.
territory: The abandoned Delray industrial district in Detroit, centered on a condemned auto manufacturing plant.
methods: Augment theft — raiding clinics, hijacking shipments, stripping chrome from victims
Chop-shop surgery — black-market augment installation at discount prices in unsanitary conditions
Mercenary violence — hiring out as shock troops, relying on their augmented durability and pain tolerance
Recruitment through addiction — offering free augments to the desperate, creating dependence
Terror — their appearance and reputation precede them, and they cultivate fear deliberately
resources: A functioning (if horrifying) surgical facility with stolen medical equipment
Stockpiles of stolen augments in various conditions
Heavily augmented members with combat-grade modifications, even if degrading
The Delray plant — large, defensible, and in territory nobody else wants
A steady supply of desperate clients willing to accept chop-shop risks
story_hooks: A Rust Prophet stole a military-grade neural interface that's degrading their brain — they're becoming something new and dangerous
Someone's loved one joined the Prophets and needs extraction before the next round of surgery kills them
The Architect claims to have achieved full-body replacement and is still conscious — is it true, or is it a puppet?
A batch of stolen augments the Prophets are installing is booby-trapped with corporate kill-switches
The Prophets are planning a mass raid on a legitimate augment clinic, which would destabilize chrome supply across Detroit
